title.raw: Lymphedema and Lymphoedema: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment
title.rendered: Lymphedema and Lymphoedema: Causes, Symptoms, and Treatment

content.raw:
Short answer: Lymphedema, also spelled lymphoedema, is persistent swelling caused by impaired lymphatic drainage. Good care starts with confirming the diagnosis, excluding other causes of swelling and matching treatment to disease stage.

Singapore treatment pathway: If you are comparing lymphedema or lymphoedema treatment in Singapore, start with the main lymphedema treatment guide. Patients who may need imaging or surgery can also review LVA / lymphovenous bypass surgery in Singapore, lymphedema surgery options, and private lymphedema specialist consultation.

Clinically reviewed by Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa, Plastic, Reconstructive & Lymphedema Surgeon in Singapore. Last reviewed: August 2026. This article is for education only and does not replace personalised medical assessment.

Common symptoms

  • persistent swelling of an arm, leg, trunk, breast or genital region;
  • heaviness, tightness or aching;
  • reduced movement or difficulty with clothing and shoes;
  • skin thickening in later stages;
  • recurrent cellulitis or infection.

Common causes

Lymphedema may occur after lymph node surgery, radiotherapy, cancer treatment, infection, trauma or congenital lymphatic problems. It can also coexist with venous disease, obesity, reduced mobility or lipedema.

Diagnosis

Assessment includes history, examination, limb pattern, skin changes, cancer treatment history, infection history and review of other causes of swelling. Imaging such as ICG lymphography, ultrasound or lymphoscintigraphy may be used in selected patients.

Treatment options

  • compression garments or bandaging;
  • complete decongestive therapy and manual lymphatic drainage;
  • exercise, skin care and weight management where relevant;
  • treatment of cellulitis and prevention of skin breakdown;
  • selected surgery such as LVA / LVB, lymph node transfer or reductive procedures.

When to seek medical advice

Seek review for persistent swelling, sudden worsening, fever, spreading redness, pain, wounds, or recurrent infection. Early assessment is especially important after cancer treatment involving lymph nodes.

Frequently asked questions

Is lymphedema the same as water retention?

No. It is related to lymphatic drainage impairment, although other fluid-retention causes may coexist.

Can treatment cure it?

Most treatment improves control rather than providing a complete cure.

Who should assess it?

The right clinician depends on the cause. Persistent or complex swelling may need lymphedema therapy, vascular assessment, cancer follow-up or lymphatic surgery review.

Related surgical guide: If swelling remains persistent despite appropriate conservative care, or if recurrent cellulitis is a major issue, read LVA surgery in Singapore: lymphovenous bypass for lymphedema.
